payload.title: agent_signals default TTL (120 min) is HALF the alert-commander-critical sweep cadence (240 min) — high-impact signals are purged before the only consumer that gates on them can read them
payload.summary: chain_catalyst / legal_risk / crisis_velocity / verified_chain / price_anomaly signals are written with a 120-minute TTL and hard-deleted at expiry. The alert-commander-critical slot that gates on exactly those types runs every 240 minutes. Any such signal posted more than 2h before the next sweep is purged unseen. On average ~50% of them can never reach the alert surface; a signal posted immediately after a sweep is invisible for its entire lifetime.

writer.detail: expires ?? expiresAt(ttlMinutes ?? 120) — repeated at lines 550, 584, 614, 641, 668. Default TTL = 120 min for every signal type except urgent_news.
writer.note: Line 154 documents the one deliberate exception: 'urgent_news signals: 240 minutes (4 hours) when this field is omitted.' The TTL-vs-cadence alignment was reasoned about ONCE, for urgent_news only, and never generalised to the types alert-commander actually gates on.

reader.detail: Line 827 comment: 'Always filters out expired signals (expires_at <= now).' Enforced at lines 915, 1252, 1429 via AND expires_at > datetime('now').
reader.purge: Line 1130 — DELETE FROM agent_signals WHERE expires_at < datetime('now'). Expired signals are not merely hidden, they are removed.

root_cause.arithmetic: TTL 120 min < cadence 240 min. Blind window = 240 - 120 = 120 min per 4h cycle = 50% of the timeline.

evidence: news-scout cycle c199 posted signal #9340 CHAIN_CATALYST 'Giá vàng vọt tăng' impact 10/10 bearish at 12:13:25Z, expiry 2026-07-25 14:13:25.
news-scout posted #9341 CHAIN_CATALYST 'Trung Nam bond 2.300 tỷ' impact 9/10 bullish at 12:13:29Z, expiry 2026-07-25 14:13:29.
Both expiries are exactly created_at + 120 min, confirming the ttlMinutes ?? 120 default is what live callers get.
alert-commander-critical last fired 12:13Z; next fire ~16:13Z. Both signals expire 14:13Z — purged 2h BEFORE the next sweep. Neither will ever be read by the alert surface.

Independent second failure the same tick: alert-commander swept at 12:13 and reported 'No chain_catalyst/legal_risk/crisis_velocity/verified_chain/price_anomaly signals in the bus this window' — it read microseconds before news-scout's write committed. Race and TTL are two distinct mechanisms producing the same blindness.
Router verified both planes rather than one: writer TTL constant AND reader expiry predicate AND purge statement all read from source at 2026-07-25T12:19Z.
blast_radius: The 4h CRITICAL-always sweep — the system's only real-time alert surface — is structurally blind to ~half of all high-impact signals produced.

Highest-impact signals are the most affected: news-scout posts chain_catalyst only for its top-scoring impacts (10/10 and 9/10 today), so the signals most likely to be purged unseen are precisely the ones most worth alerting on.

Directly extends docs/signals/router-alert-commander-dead-20260703.md. That signal restored a DEAD consumer (missing cowork slot, ~5.5 weeks silent, PNJ coverage miss). The consumer is now alive and running — but still cannot see the producer's output. The 07-03 fix addressed reachability of the agent; this addresses reachability of the data. Closing one without the other leaves the original user-visible symptom intact.
Explains alert-commander silent-exiting on days when news-scout demonstrably produced high-impact chain_catalyst signals — silence reads as 'nothing happened' when it may mean 'everything expired'.
secondary_findings: get_agent_signals appears to mark rows read on read. Router's diagnostic query at 12:19Z returned #9340/#9341 with status 'read'. This did NOT suppress them (alert-commander's own 12:13 sweep also returned read-status rows, so the reader does not filter unread-only), but a read-marking diagnostic is a side-effecting one and should be treated as such. Flagged in the spirit of the standing 'read-only ≠ no-POST' lesson.

news-scout c199 identified 'PNJ crisis 8/10 bearish — liquidity stress, control transfer' and 'Oil/yields 9/10 bullish' as impacts but posted NEITHER as a signal (only gold 10 and bond 9 reached the bus). The posting predicate is not a clean impact threshold — 9/10 oil was identified and dropped while 9/10 bond was posted. UNVERIFIED: router did not read the news-scout posting gate. Worth a separate look, especially as PNJ is the same ticker as the 07-03 coverage-miss incident.
alert-commander reported get_foreign_room exceeding the max-token response limit (72,409 chars) and skipping it — a standing, separately-tracked token-overflow gap, non-blocking this cycle.
alert-commander reported get_macro_calendar() returning status 'unavailable' with no events, forcing pivot_window_active=false.
payload.suggested_fix_direction: Do NOT simply raise the global default to 240. Two candidate framings for PO: (a) make TTL a function of the consumer cadence — any signal type gated by a scheduled sweep must carry TTL >= that sweep's cadence, ideally >= 2x for one guaranteed overlap, mirroring what urgent_news already does deliberately at 240; or (b) decouple consumption from expiry — have the sweep read a durable high-water-mark of signals-since-last-sweep rather than a live TTL window, which removes the whole class of cadence-vs-TTL coupling. (b) is the definitive fix and also closes the 12:13 read/write race, which (a) does not. Recommend (b) with (a) as the cheap interim. Whichever is chosen, the alert-commander-critical cadence-policy gap noted in the sibling 12:14Z signal should be resolved in the same pass, since that slot currently has zero policy rows and silently inherits the 240-min default that this bug is measured against.
payload.router_scope_note: Router is dispatcher-only and did not modify apps/**, mint a board row, or alter any schedule. Verification was read-only against source; the single live tool call (get_agent_signals) is disclosed above as read-marking.
